why: Both cover April Fools fakes and reactions to them, and the batch's r/runescape items split fakes the room staged from the company's claims being tested.

why.T3-033: Most concepts offer the room an idea of what to make (gnome, GET BOND, construction icon, Guthix symbol, r/runescape label) and call the room to it, which is proposing the mark, not a call to a mark already chosen or a spot searched for.

why.T3-001: The room's own members post false things as true for April Fools (new skill, pizza instead of bonds, rainbow cape, bankstanding pet, UnScape) and others play along or admit being caught, which is staging the room's own fakes, not testing an outside claim.

why.T3-100: Members ask that April Fools joke rewards outlive the day: the Clerk pet, the Min-Cape, the Green Partyhat, a real bank-interface chance, which is asking to keep or make real a joke feature, not judging it on the day.

why.T3-032: Many concepts object to the April Fools posts in the sub itself: reposts counted, 'pls can thls st0p', r/repost, the flood said to be stale, tellers told they are 11 posts late, so the room objects to its own joke posts.
why.T3-048: A distinct set judges Jagex's own jokes as jokes: 'lame ass april fools jagex I r8 2/8', the joke 'kinda dry', 'not funny', 'Best April Fools by far', which is a verdict on the maker's joke, not on posts in the sub.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: A single T3-032 placement registers the objection to the sub's joke posts but would not carry the strands that judge the company's own prank for quality or compare it with other years, which are talk about the maker's joke rather than posts in the sub.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0028280 rates Jagex's April Fools '2/8', C1352430 calls the bankstanding joke dry, C0459467 says 'not funny', C0820649 calls it the best by far, which satisfy T3-048's gate of judging the maker's joke.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-048 would be dropped if forced to one; what would be lost is the room's verdict on Jagex's prank itself as distinct from its policing of the sub's posts.

why.T3-095: Members settle whether claims they did not stage are real or jokes: the rainbow cape, Get Bond changing to Get Pizza, fake broadcasts, the fake ring image exposed by zooming, checking JagexAuto, which is testing outside claims rather than playing inside the room's own fakes.

why.T3-001: These are replies inside fakes and reports of being caught by them: waking a brother over a fake broadcast, thinking an alt was hacked, 'Well, that fooled me', which is being caught by the room's own April Fools fakes, not testing an outside claim.

why.T3-043: After placement the theme credits those who kept it: thanks to all for keeping the dream alive and calling participation an honor, which is crediting the defenders and makers rather than celebrating the image as such.

why.T3-031: The room's own meme is played in canvas talk: Dat Boi explained as the self-made meme pulled from the void, backed as reserve currency of the meme economy with a tear, which is the room's running joke carried in talk rather than an attack fought.

why.T3-016: Members ask and answer what r/place is and how it works: the one-pixel-per-five-minutes rule, banding together to draw and maintain, which is explaining the event itself rather than the room's own coordinates or a picture's meaning.

why.T3-095: An ordinary-looking announcement (the documentary launch) is immediately tested against the date and refused as a possible April Fools trick, which is settling whether a claim the room did not stage is a joke.

why.T3-043: Members give and contest credit for the drawings: OSRS said to have commissioned the meme and gnome child head, 2007scape holding positions, the script credited to r/Two101, RS3 versus OSRS ownership disputed, which is crediting and contesting who made the work.

why.T3-002: Between placements members call in more hands: going to advertise on r/place for manpower, and using every cooldown to negotiate or advertise for manpower, which is calling placers in to place rather than asking a kindred sub as a group.

why.T3-009: Many concepts mark the room's work as achieved: 'WE DID IT', 'our little logo is pretty much intact. Well done', 'WE ARE IMMORTALISED!', pride in the defence and the corner claimed.
why.T3-073: A distinct set tells what happened to the work once it stood: Connection Lost nearly 100% intact except a couple of pixels, the missing periods corrected, the endless battle to remove extra periods, which is reporting how the work fared rather than celebrating it.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: A single T3-009 placement marks the work as achieved but would not carry the reports of what befell it (pixels off target, missing periods, the fight over extra periods), which are an account of the work's fate rather than a celebration.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1521615 reports the Connection Lost banner nearly intact at the end, C0619936 checks neighbouring art's condition, C1237692 recalls someone turning a corner purple and adding ellipses, C0078015 recalls the endless battle to remove the extra periods, satisfying T3-073's gate of reporting what happened to the work.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-073 would be dropped if forced to one; what would be lost is the item's account of the work's fate as distinct from its celebration.

why.T3-015: Members and moderators gather scattered canvas talk into one place: redirecting helpers to the strategy thread, deleting duplicates and moving discussion to the original, stickying a hub and sending a proposal there, which is routing canvas posts into a megathread.

why.T3-016: Members ask and answer what r/place is and how it works: one tile every five minutes per user, banding together to draw and maintain against vandalism, which is explaining the event itself.
